chunks: And from the hadith of Mu'ammār ibn Sulaymān, who said: I heard Ismā'īl ibn Abī Khālid narrating from Mujālid, from ash-Sha'bī, from Jābir ibn Samurah, from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).

He said: 'This religion will remain prominent, unaffected by its opponents, until twelve Caliphs have passed.' Then he said a word that I did not understand. I asked my father: 'What did he say?' He said: 'He said: All of them are from Quraysh.'
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about the number and lineage of the Caliphs?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded by al-Nu'mani, outlines the Prophet's (SAW) prophecy regarding the continuity of Islamic authority through twelve Caliphs, all from the tribe of Quraysh. In Shia scholarship, this is often interpreted as a reference to the twelve Imams, emphasizing their divine appointment and Qurayshi lineage, while Sunni traditions typically view it as referring to the first twelve caliphs or a specific period of leadership. The clarification by the narrator's father underscores the significance of tribal legitimacy in early Islamic governance.
